All manners: the report says these deaths 'may be accidents, suicides or homicides', so not unintentional-only and not an ICD-10 W65-W74 count. Boating drownings are not separated. The OCME takes jurisdiction over deaths not known to be due to exclusively natural processes; residency is not stated. No place or activity split is printed.

notes: Five rows, one per year 2020-2024, all from the Maine Office of Chief Medical Examiner annual reports on DigitalMaine (the Attorney General's documents collection). Definition: the OCME prints drowning as a 'mode of death' in an untitled four-column table (Firearm / Drowning / Child (<2 years) / Fire Related) and says these deaths 'may be accidents, suicides or homicides', so the counts cover ALL manners (and presumably undetermined), unlike CDC's unintentional W65-W74/V90/V92 series behind us-cdc-4345, us-cdc-4500 and us-total-2022. Water-transport drownings are neither separated nor excluded. The OCME takes jurisdiction over 'all deaths that are not known to be due to exclusively natural processes'; whether non-residents dying in Maine are included, or Maine residents dying elsewhere excluded, is not stated, so the series is best read as drownings investigated by the Maine OCME. No place or activity split is printed in any edition opened, so no setting rows could be returned; the lab's by-water question for Maine stays open (see next_tasks). Values as printed: 2020 = 43 (2020 edition p. 9; 2023 edition p. 11), 2021 = 29, 2022 = 31, 2023 = 31 (both the 2023 and 2024 editions), 2024 = 26 (2024 edition p. 10). The tables carry no caption, footnote or provisional flag; the 2023 and 2024 editions were posted on DigitalMaine on 13 Aug 2026, the 2020 edition on 1 Jul 2021. Values read by eye from the fetch tool's PDF text; the reviewer should open p. 10 of the 2024 report and p. 9 of the 2020 report to confirm the column order (the fetch tool reported the headers in that order). The pie-chart shares (drowning 2% of accidental deaths in 2024, 4% in 2020) are not recorded as rows because the label-to-value pairing was inferred from label order. Row ids follow the ledger's '<place>-total-<year>' style; a future Maine vital-statistics (ICD W65-W74) series should take a different id stem (for example maine-residents-w65-w74-<year>) because the definitions differ. Comparison rows: nothing to correct in uscg-boating-2024 from what was read. For us-cdc-4345: the CDC Drowning Data page as fetched on 21 Oct 2026 read 'over 4,000' fatal unintentional drownings a year, with a footnote averaging 4,083 for 2012-2021, and described the state map as 2018-2021 rates; the ledger row says 4,345 for 2018-2021 from the page dated 27 Jan 2026. One fetch cannot tell whether the page changed or the tool returned another version, so no correction is proposed; a verify follow-up is listed instead. Budget: about 26 searches and fetches. VERIFICATION 21 Oct 2026: all five original rows confirmed in at least two editions each; column alignment is pinned by each edition's own change sentences (2023: child deaths fell 33 to 22 while drowning stayed 31; 2025: child fell 18 to 12 while drowning rose 26 to 37). The 2025 edition exists and prints drowning = 37, added as maine-total-2025 (needs an eye check: its firearm value looks anomalous). The 2020 and 2023 edition page numbers may be one lower than the PDF page markers.
